_comment: Per-provider tool-name rewrite rules + idiom translation notes applied to agent and command bodies at render time. Source bodies use Claude Code tool names (capitalized) and Claude idioms (e.g. 'Load skills/X/SKILL.md', 'spawn the agent at .claude/agents/dev-team/X.md'). The renderer uses tool_rewrites to describe the tool-name mapping, and idiom_notes to describe the brighter conventions for skill loading and subagent spawning.

claude._comment: Identity — source already uses Claude Code tool names and idioms.

opencode._comment: opencode exposes lowercase tool names; the `task` tool spawns subagents; `question` is the quiz tool. Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep/Bash stay lowercase. Skills are loaded via the `skill` tool named `SKILL.md` filename form (e.g. `skill({ name: 'reviewer-mindset' })`). Subagents are spawned via `task({ name: '<agent-name>' })` — no path arg, the name only.
idiom_notes: · **Skill loading.** When the body says `Load skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md`, invoke the opencode `skill` tool with the skill's folder name, e.g. `skill({ name: '<name>' })`. The skill body lives at `.opencode/skills/dev-team-agents/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md` and opencode resolves it by name.

· **Subagent spawn.** When the body says `spawn the agent at .claude/agents/dev-team/<X>.md`, treat it as `task({ name: '<X>' })` in opencode — subagents are registered as `.opencode/agents/<X>.md` and resolved by name only, no path.

· **Project context paths.** References like `docs/`, `.dev-team-agents/user-data/preferences.json`, `.dev-team-agents/scripts/...` are real paths materialized at install time; access them with the `read` tool the same way Claude would.

codex._comment: Codex uses function-calling tool names: apply_patch (file edits, aliases Edit/Write), spawn_agent (subagent invocation, alias Agent), update_plan (plan/todos), WebSearch (hosted web search). Codex has no structured quiz tool — AskUserQuestion falls back to plain-text question. Skills load is done via `apply_patch` to Read the SKILL.md path; subagent spawn via `spawn_agent({ agent_type: '<name>' })`.
codex._post_render_note: Bodies using _plain_text_question_ get a `**NOTE for Codex port**: this question should be asked as plain text; Codex has no structured quiz tool.` appended inline by the renderer.
idiom_notes: · **Tool names.** Throughout this body, Claude Code tool names are used. Replace them:
· `AskUserQuestion` → plain text question (Codex has no quiz tool)
· `Glob` / `Grep` → `Bash` (Codex has no dedicated search tools); use shell commands instead.

· **Skill loading.** When the body says `Load skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md`, Read the file at path `.dev-team-agents/skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md` using `apply_patch` in Read mode. Codex has no dedicated skill tool.

· **Subagent spawn.** When the body says `spawn the agent at .claude/agents/dev-team/<X>.md`, use `spawn_agent({ agent_type: '<X>' })`. The agent definition lives at `.codex/agents/<X>.toml` — resolved by name, not path.

· **Project context paths.** References like `docs/some-file.md`, `.dev-team-agents/user-data/preferences.json`, `.dev-team-agents/scripts/...` are real files in this project. Read them with `apply_patch` (Read mode).

· **Plan gate.** Commands marked with a plan gate: use Codex's native plan mode when the task is complex or architectural. For simple tasks, execute directly. The `update_plan` tool is Codex's equivalent of presenting a plan.
· **Task arguments.** `$ARGUMENTS` in command bodies represents the user's free-form input after the slash command. Use it as the task description.
